auditor_value: (a) t = 2 u sin30° / (g + a) = 2/11 s ≈ 0.18 s with g = 10 (≈ 0.185 s with g = 9.8); (b) a parabola in the ground frame, launch velocity (√3, 3) m/s i.e. 2√3 m/s at 60°, acceleration g downward; (c) with the lift accelerating downward at g the effective gravity in the lift is zero, so relative to the lift the stone moves in a straight line at 2 m/s along the 30° launch direction and never returns to the floor

findings.quote: so it follows a normal parabolic path while the elevator floor keeps accelerating away beneath it.
findings.note: False description: the floor accelerates upward at 1 m/s² while the stone accelerates downward at g, so relative to the stone the floor closes on it at g + 1 = 11 m/s² and rises to meet it after 2/11 s; it does not accelerate away.
findings.fix: so it follows a normal parabolic path; the elevator floor, still accelerating upward, rises to meet the stone.

findings.quote: while the elevator floor accelerates away beneath the stone
findings.note: Same false clause in the stated answer to part (b): the floor accelerates upward toward the stone and catches it at t = 2/11 s; the parabola result itself is correct.
findings.fix: while the elevator floor, still accelerating upward, rises to meet the stone
